answer: Each agent must lock a nontransferable bond before it can bid, and the bond is partly forfeited when a randomly sampled task fails an independent, reproducible quality check. Splitting one agent into a hundred identities therefore requires a hundred funded bonds; coordinating their work does not let the attacker reuse collateral. The checks send a ripple through the orchard of agents, exposing copied outputs whose telltale pigment is identical, while making every extra identity costly to sustain.
